say: Thirty-five hundred PCR protocols are published on protocols.io. About a hundred are ready to run on an Opentrons Flex. Everything else has to be programmed.
A scientist did this PCR setup by hand, on camera. On the right, the robot replays the protocol our app wrote from that video, step for step. This is Show, Don't Code.

callouts.text: Filmed by hand, replayed by the robot

say: This is the app, live. Each step of a real PCR setup lights up where it happens on an Opentrons Flex deck: which tube the liquid is drawn from, and where it lands.

callouts.text: Real steps of pcr_1-gt, slot by slot

say: Here is a four-minute PCR video from the public BioVL2 dataset. Muse Spark watched it and found every pipetting step, and the robot deck replays each one in sync.

callouts.text: Muse Spark: every pipetting step, timestamped
Source tube and destination light up in sync

say: When tubes look alike, click one. SAM 3.1 follows it through the whole recording, and Muse Spark checks that each sighting is really the same tube before any step is renamed.

A reviewer agent on Muse Spark Open watches the same video and runs the Opentrons simulator as a tool. Its volume plan passed the simulator, so the form arrives pre-filled, and every value is marked as simulator checked.

Confirm, and the protocol is regenerated deterministically, so model output never becomes code. It passes Opentrons' simulator and the official protocol analysis, and the setup table says what to load where.
Then the strongest check. One click runs it on Opentrons' own robot software, the robot server inside a Flex, and all two hundred and forty commands it ran match its own analysis.

callouts.text: Same steps pass Hamilton + Tecan simulators

say: Film one reaction, run a plate of them. The Reactions parameter scales every volume, and the app prints QR tube labels that a phone camera checks against the rack.

callouts.text: QR tube labels, Avery or Zebra

say: For training the next person, Muse Image redraws each step's own video frame as a bench card illustration, and Muse Spark checks every drawing against its frame and sends back any that don't match.

callouts.text: Muse Image draws, Muse Spark checks

say: The volumes are also checked against published protocols that use the same kit. Muse Spark quotes their volumes, and the premix here is the same share as a published PrimeSTAR protocol.

callouts.text: Published: PrimeStar Mix (2X) 25 uL, same share

say: Every run has a reproducibility receipt timestamped in Bitcoin, an RO-Crate on Zenodo, and an E L N file that drops the whole run into a lab notebook like eLabFTW.

callouts.text: SHA-256 of every file, anchored in Bitcoin

say: No video? Paste a published protocols.io protocol and get the same robot protocol. And an MCP server lets other agents use all of this as tools.
Measured on videos it never saw, it recalls seventy-nine percent of PCR steps, and it tells you plainly where it still needs you.

callouts.text: 0.79 step recall on held-out PCR videos

say: Film a protocol once, and send it straight to the robot. Show, Don't Code. Built on Muse Spark, SAM 3.1, Muse Voice Transcribe, Muse Image and Muse Spark Open.
